title: Concentration of a biased Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $p\in[0,1]$, let $S\subseteq[n]$, and let $t\ge0$. Choose a random function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ by assigning independent values, each equal to $1$ with probability $p$ and $0$ otherwise. The probability that the absolute difference between its $S$-th Fourier coefficient and $p$ when $S=\varnothing$, or $0$ otherwise, is at least $t$ is at most $2\exp\!\left(-2^n t^2/2\right)$.
